subject.title: [Bug]: agents.defaults.compaction.* reload is classified as a no-op but the value is captured per process — edits silently never apply

question: Should `agents.defaults.compaction.*` be supported as a true hot-reload surface, or should process-captured compaction settings explicitly require a Gateway restart?
rationale: Both choices alter the documented operator contract: hot reload requires proving every active compaction consumer receives the refreshed configuration, while restart-required is safer but changes the current misleading no-op behavior.

options.title: Require restart for captured compaction settings
options.body: Classify the affected paths as restart-required and log that a gateway restart is needed, avoiding partial runtime propagation.

options.title: Make compaction settings fully hot-reloadable
options.body: Refresh the runtime configuration through the compaction execution path and add coverage for active-session behavior after an edit.

options.title: Read these values lazily at compaction time
options.body: Redesign compaction setting lookup so these paths can remain no-ops because each compaction observes the canonical current configuration.

recommendation.title: Require restart for captured compaction settings
recommendation.body: Classify the affected paths as restart-required and log that a gateway restart is needed, avoiding partial runtime propagation.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the clearest observed production reproduction and can validate the resulting operator-facing behavior; code-history ownership needs a separate source pass.
